question: When did Ahaziah begin to reign?
summary: 2 Kings 8:25 dates Ahaziah's accession to the twelfth year of Joram king of Israel. 2 Kings 9:29 dates the same accession to the eleventh year of Joram. The two notices contradict each other within the same book, four chapters apart.

reconcile.connective: Defenders read the two dates as one accession told two ways — a co-regency begun in Joram's eleventh year, sole rule in his twelfth.

discrepancy.connective: Steve Wells (Skeptic's Annotated Bible) presses the plain arithmetic — the same accession is dated to two different years of Joram, and notes that textual scholars read the eleventh-year notice as a later correction of the twelfth.

excerpts.attribution: Adam Clarke, Commentary on the Bible (1832)
excerpts.excerpt_text: Then he began to reign as viceroy to his father in his sickness; Ch2 21:18, Ch2 21:19. But in Joram's twelfth year he began to reign alone; Kg2 8:26.
excerpts.on_tension_rationale: Clarke names both notices and resolves the eleventh-vs-twelfth-year gap by distinguishing Ahaziah's co-regency (viceroy during his father's terminal illness) from his sole reign — the strongest single harmonization on the row.
excerpts.source_note_text: In the eleventh year of Joram - The note in our margin contains as good an account of this chronological difficulty as can be reasonably required: Then he began to reign as viceroy to his father in his sickness; Ch2 21:18, Ch2 21:19. But in Joram's twelfth year he began to reign alone; Kg2 8:26.
